modules.name: ShortenService
modules.responsibility: Create short codes for long URLs, validate input URLs, enforce uniqueness, and resolve codes back to original URLs.

modules.name: CodeGenerator
modules.responsibility: Produce collision-resistant short codes from an internal id or random source (base62 encoding).

modules.name: RedirectController
modules.responsibility: Handle inbound GET /{code} requests, resolve the code, emit a click event, and return an HTTP redirect or 404.
interfaces:
class RedirectController(Protocol):
    def handle(self, code: str, ctx: RequestContext) -> RedirectResponse: ...

modules.name: StatsRecorder
modules.responsibility: Record click events asynchronously and aggregate click statistics per short code.

modules.name: RateLimiter
modules.responsibility: Enforce per-client request budgets on shorten and redirect endpoints using a fixed/sliding window counter.
interfaces:
class RateLimiter(Protocol):
    def check(self, key: str, *, cost: int = 1) -> RateDecision: ...

modules.name: Persistence
modules.responsibility: Abstract storage for links, click events, and rate-limit counters behind narrow store Protocols.
interfaces:
class LinkStore(Protocol):
    def put(self, link: ShortLink) -> None: ...
    def get(self, code: str) -> ShortLink | None: ...
    def exists(self, code: str) -> bool: ...

class CounterStore(Protocol):
    def incr(self, key: str, ttl: int) -> int: ...

ux_flows.name: Shorten a URL
steps: CodeGenerator produces unique code (retry on collision)
ux_flows.success_criteria: Caller receives a working short URL in a single request (<200ms p95)
i18n_considerations: Error messages localized via message catalog

ux_flows.name: Follow a short link
steps: If found and not expired, StatsRecorder.record(click) fired async
ux_flows.success_criteria: Visitor redirected to original URL with no perceptible delay

ux_flows.name: View click statistics
steps: AuthZ check (owner token or public-stats flag)
ux_flows.success_criteria: Owner sees accurate total + unique + per-day counts

customer_journey: A user with a long, unwieldy URL submits it to the service (via API or CLI) and instantly receives a compact short link they can paste anywhere. When anyone clicks that link, they are transparently redirected to the original destination while the service records the click in the background without slowing the redirect. Later, the link's owner queries the stats endpoint and sees how many times the link was clicked, how many unique visitors hit it, and the trend over days. Throughout, abusive or runaway clients are throttled by rate limiting so the service stays fast and available for everyone. Privacy is respected: IPs are hashed, not stored raw, and links/clicks can be erased on request.

experience_metric.name: shorten_to_link_steps
experience_metric.target: Obtain a working short URL in ≤1 API call and follow it in ≤1 redirect hop

architecture_decisions.title: Asynchronous click recording decoupled from the redirect path
architecture_decisions.context: Redirects must be fast and resilient. Writing a click record synchronously couples redirect latency and availability to the stats store; a slow or down stats backend would degrade or break the core redirect function.
architecture_decisions.decision: Fire ClickEvents through a StatsRecorder that records out-of-band (in-process queue / background worker), and perform the redirect before/independent of the record completing. Stats accuracy is eventually consistent.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Redirect is the critical, highest-traffic path and must satisfy SRP: it resolves and redirects, nothing more. Decoupling honors the single-responsibility and dependency-inversion principles, keeps redirect p95 low, and isolates failures in the stats subsystem.
consequences: Stats are eventually consistent, not real-time exact
Need a durable buffer or accept best-effort loss on crash
StatsRecorder must be independently testable and swappable

architecture_decisions.title: Base62 random codes over sequential-id encoding
architecture_decisions.context: Short codes can be generated by encoding a monotonic id or by random generation. Sequential ids leak total link count and are enumerable.
architecture_decisions.decision: Generate random base62 codes of configurable length with a uniqueness check + bounded retry, behind a CodeGenerator Protocol.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Non-enumerable codes prevent scraping/competitor intelligence and resource enumeration while keeping codes short. The Protocol keeps the strategy swappable.
consequences: Slightly less dense than pure sequential encoding

threat_model.description: Open redirect abuse: attacker shortens a URL pointing to a malicious/phishing site and leverages the trusted short domain to bypass user suspicion.
threat_model.mitigation: Validate scheme (http/https only), optional domain allow/deny lists, malware/phishing blocklist check at creation, and an interstitial warning page for flagged links.

threat_model.description: Flood of shorten or redirect requests exhausts storage or compute, degrading availability for all users.
threat_model.mitigation: Per-client (ip_hash) sliding-window rate limiting with 429 responses, plus global circuit-breaker caps and cheap cached redirect lookups.

threat_model.description: Enumeration of short codes or stats endpoints reveals others' links and click data (PII in click logs).
threat_model.mitigation: Random non-sequential codes, authorization on stats endpoint, IP hashing (never raw IPs), and rate-limited lookups to slow enumeration.

privacy_inventory.purpose: Abuse detection, unique-visitor counting, rate-limit keying
privacy_inventory.retention: Never stored raw; only salted SHA-256 hash retained 90 days then purged
privacy_inventory.encryption: Salted one-way hash at ingest; at-rest encryption on store
privacy_inventory.erasure_path: Delete click events for a code; rotate salt to invalidate hashes

privacy_inventory.retention: Lifetime of link or until expiry/erasure request
privacy_inventory.erasure_path: DELETE /api/links/{code} removes link and cascades click events

i18n_plan.rtl_strategy: Logical CSS properties + dir=auto on error/landing pages; mirror layout for ar/he
i18n_plan.datetime: UTC storage, locale + timezone formatting at presentation
i18n_plan.notes: Accept IDN/punycode hostnames in input URLs

open_questions: Do short links expire by default, and if so what is the TTL policy?
Is link ownership authenticated (accounts/API keys) or anonymous with capability tokens for stats?
What is the durability requirement for click events — is best-effort loss on crash acceptable, or is a durable queue required?
Should the rate limiter be in-process (single node) or distributed (Redis) for multi-instance deployment?
Are custom aliases supported at launch, and what is the reserved-word/profanity policy?

sections.title: Module Boundaries
sections.content: Six modules: ShortenService (create/resolve), CodeGenerator (base62), RedirectController (GET /{code}), StatsRecorder (async clicks), RateLimiter (window counters), Persistence (LinkStore/ClickStore/CounterStore Protocols). All collaborators injected for DIP/testability.

sections.title: Data Model
sections.content: ShortLink(code pk, long_url, custom_alias?, created_at, creator_ip_hash?, expires_at?). ClickEvent(id, code fk, timestamp, ip_hash?, user_agent?, referrer?, country?) classified PII. ClickStats derived aggregate. RateCounter for limiting. IPs always hashed.

sections.title: UX Flows
sections.content: Shorten (POST /api/shorten -> short_url), Redirect (GET /{code} -> 301/302 + async click), View Stats (GET /api/stats/{code}). Error states cover 400/404/409/410/429. Metric: working short URL in ≤1 call, redirect p95 ≤50ms.

sections.title: Architecture Decisions
sections.content: ADR-001 decouples click recording from the redirect path for latency/resilience (eventually consistent stats). ADR-002 chooses random base62 codes over sequential ids to prevent enumeration/volume leakage.

sections.title: Threats & Privacy
sections.content: Top threats: open-redirect abuse (validation+blocklist), DoS (rate limiting+caching), enumeration/info disclosure (random codes+authz). PII = visitor IP, stored only as salted hash, 90-day retention, erasure via cascade delete + salt rotation.
